theme: Games with no element of chance: no dice, card draws, or blind tile pulls, so outcomes depend only on the players' decisions.

members.title: Chess
members.description: Two armies of sixteen pieces maneuver across an 8x8 checkered board.

members.title: Go
members.description: Stones are placed alternately on a grid to surround territory.

members.title: Checkers
members.description: Discs move diagonally and capture by jumping over opponents.

members.title: Othello
members.description: Discs flip between two colors when outflanked along a line.

members.title: Connect Four
members.description: Drop discs into a vertical rack to line up four in a row.

members.title: Hive
members.description: Hexagonal insect pieces form the playing surface as they are placed.

members.title: Nine Men's Morris
members.description: Form rows of three on nested squares to remove enemy pieces.

members.title: Abalone
members.description: Marbles shove each other off the edge of a hexagonal board.

members.title: Oware
members.description: Seeds are sown around a ring of pits, capturing on certain counts.

intruders.title: Backgammon
intruders.description: Race fifteen checkers around triangular points and bear them off.
intruders.why: Every move is dictated by a roll of two dice.

intruders.title: Scrabble
intruders.description: Build interlocking words on a grid of premium squares for points.
intruders.why: Letter tiles are drawn blind from a bag, so each rack is luck.

theme: Kitchen tools that work by cutting: a blade or sharp edge severs the food.
decoy: Handheld gadgets for preparing produce and ingredients

members.title: Mandoline
members.description: Flat frame with an adjustable platform for uniform thin pieces.

members.title: Microplane zester
members.description: Long rasp that lifts fine strands from citrus peel and hard cheese.

members.title: Egg slicer
members.description: Hinged frame that divides a boiled egg into even rounds.

members.title: Pizza wheel
members.description: Rolling disc on a handle for portioning flatbreads.

members.title: Apple corer
members.description: Ringed tube pushed through fruit to remove the center.

members.title: Cheese plane
members.description: Flat spatula with a slot that shaves thin sheets from a block.

members.title: Poultry shears
members.description: Heavy spring-loaded scissors for jointing birds.

members.title: Spiralizer
members.description: Crank-turned gadget that turns vegetables into long ribbons.

members.title: Mezzaluna
members.description: Curved rocking tool with handles at both ends, used on herbs.

intruders.title: Garlic press
intruders.description: Hinged tool that forces cloves through a perforated chamber.
intruders.why: It crushes and extrudes; nothing in it has a cutting edge.

intruders.title: Potato ricer
intruders.description: Lever-operated hopper that pushes cooked potatoes through small holes.
intruders.why: It extrudes soft food through a plate rather than cutting it.

theme: Woodwind instruments: the sound comes from a reed or from air split across an edge, whatever the body is made of.

members.title: Flute
members.description: Metal tube held sideways and played by blowing over an open hole.

members.title: Saxophone
members.description: Brass-bodied conical instrument with a curved neck and upturned bell.

members.title: Clarinet
members.description: Black cylindrical instrument with a beaked mouthpiece and flared bell.

members.title: Oboe
members.description: Slender conical instrument whose pitch tunes the orchestra.

members.title: Bassoon
members.description: Tall folded instrument with a long curved metal crook.

members.title: Piccolo
members.description: Half-sized, highest-pitched voice of the orchestra's wind section.

members.title: English horn
members.description: Alto instrument with a bulb-shaped bell, pitched a fifth below its smaller sibling.

members.title: Recorder
members.description: Wooden or plastic end-blown pipe common in school music classes.

intruders.title: French horn
intruders.description: Coiled metal instrument ending in a wide bell, played with a hand inside it.
intruders.why: A brass instrument: the player's lips buzz in a cup mouthpiece. Its name echoes the English horn, which is a woodwind.

theme: Dishes named after a specific real person.
decoy: Classic restaurant dishes with proper-noun names

members.title: Peach Melba
members.description: Poached peaches with raspberry sauce over vanilla ice cream.

members.title: Pavlova
members.description: Meringue with a crisp crust and soft center, topped with fruit and cream.

members.title: Beef Stroganoff
members.description: Sauteed strips of beef in a sour-cream sauce.

members.title: Oysters Rockefeller
members.description: Baked oysters on the half shell under a rich green herb topping.

members.title: Carpaccio
members.description: Paper-thin slices of raw beef dressed with oil and shaved cheese.

members.title: Nachos
members.description: Tortilla chips baked with melted cheese and sliced jalapenos.

members.title: Caesar salad
members.description: Romaine with croutons, parmesan, and a coddled-egg dressing.

members.title: Bananas Foster
members.description: Bananas flambeed in butter, brown sugar, and rum, served over ice cream.

members.title: Salisbury steak
members.description: Seasoned ground-beef patty served in brown gravy.

members.title: Chicken Tetrazzini
members.description: Baked pasta and chicken in a creamy mushroom-and-sherry sauce.

intruders.title: Chicken Marengo
intruders.description: Chicken braised with tomatoes, garlic, and wine, garnished with crayfish.
intruders.why: Named after the Battle of Marengo, a village in Piedmont. It is tied to Napoleon but not named for him.

intruders.title: Lobster Thermidor
intruders.description: Lobster in a cognac-cream sauce, returned to the shell and browned.
intruders.why: Named after the play 'Thermidor', which takes its name from a month in the French Revolutionary calendar. No person is involved.

theme: Structures originally built for a world's fair or international exposition.

members.title: Eiffel Tower
members.description: Wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris.

members.title: Atomium
members.description: Nine steel-clad spheres joined by tubes, in Brussels.

members.title: Space Needle
members.description: Observation tower with a saucer-shaped top in Seattle.

members.title: Habitat 67
members.description: Stacked prefabricated concrete boxes forming a housing complex in Montreal.

members.title: Montreal Biosphere
members.description: Buckminster Fuller geodesic dome on an island in the St. Lawrence.

members.title: Barcelona Pavilion
members.description: Mies van der Rohe's low hall of marble, onyx, glass, and chrome columns.

members.title: Palace of Fine Arts
members.description: Roman-style rotunda and colonnade beside a lagoon in San Francisco.

members.title: Tower of the Americas
members.description: Slender concrete tower topped by a revolving restaurant in San Antonio.

members.title: Crystal Palace
members.description: Vast cast-iron and plate-glass hall first raised in Hyde Park, London.

intruders.title: Tokyo Tower
intruders.description: Orange-and-white lattice tower modeled on a famous Parisian landmark.
intruders.why: Built in 1958 as a broadcast tower, not for an exposition. It echoes the Eiffel Tower in form only.

intruders.title: Beijing National Stadium
intruders.description: Woven steel-lattice 'Bird's Nest' arena in Beijing.
intruders.why: Built for the 2008 Olympics: a major international event, but a sporting one, not an exposition.

theme: Reaction-image memes that are frames taken from a film, TV show, or TV cartoon.

members.title: One Does Not Simply
members.description: A bearded man at a council gestures while explaining why a task is harder than it sounds.

members.title: Surprised Pikachu
members.description: A yellow creature stares with its mouth hanging open in shock.

members.title: Is This a Pigeon?
members.description: A bespectacled man gestures at a butterfly and misidentifies it.

members.title: Picard Facepalm
members.description: A bald officer in uniform buries his face in his hand.

members.title: Laughing Leo
members.description: A man in a velvet jacket laughs, drink in hand, surrounded by guests.

members.title: Spider-Man Pointing
members.description: Two identical costumed heroes point accusingly at each other.

members.title: Mocking SpongeBob
members.description: A hunched sea sponge clucks, captioned in alternating capital letters.

members.title: Not Sure If
members.description: A squinting orange-haired man narrows his eyes in suspicion.

intruders.title: This Is Fine
intruders.description: A cartoon dog sips coffee calmly while the room around him burns.
intruders.why: Comes from KC Green's webcomic 'Gunshow'. It looks like a cartoon but was never on screen.

intruders.title: Distracted Boyfriend
intruders.description: A man turns to eye a passerby while his companion glares at him.
intruders.why: A staged stock photograph by Antonio Guillem. It looks cinematic but is not a film still.

theme: Games that began as fan-made mods of another game.
decoy: Influential PC multiplayer and indie games

members.title: Counter-Strike
members.description: Tactical team shooter: one side plants a bomb, the other defuses it.

members.title: Defense of the Ancients
members.description: Three-lane battle in which each player commands a single hero.

members.title: DayZ
members.description: Survivors scavenge a post-Soviet countryside overrun by the infected.

members.title: Team Fortress
members.description: Class-based team shooter built around capturing flags.

members.title: Garry's Mod
members.description: Physics sandbox for building contraptions, with no set goals.

members.title: The Stanley Parable
members.description: An office worker defies a narrator in a branching story.

members.title: Dear Esther
members.description: Wander an empty Hebridean island while a narrator reads letters.

members.title: Red Orchestra
members.description: Unforgiving Eastern Front infantry shooter.

members.title: Day of Defeat
members.description: Second World War squad shooter fought over control points.

intruders.title: League of Legends
intruders.description: Two teams of five champions push lanes toward the enemy base.
intruders.why: Built from scratch as a standalone commercial game. It was inspired by DotA but was never a mod itself.

intruders.title: Fortnite
intruders.description: Hundred-player last-one-standing shooter where you build cover on the fly.
intruders.why: Epic built its battle royale mode in-house. The genre traces back to mods, but this game did not start as one.

theme: Products first made or sold for a completely different use than the one they became famous for.
decoy: Everyday products with well-known invention stories

members.title: Bubble Wrap
members.description: Sheets of air-filled plastic cushions.

members.title: Play-Doh
members.description: Soft, brightly colored modeling compound for children.

members.title: Kleenex
members.description: Disposable facial tissues pulled from a box.

members.title: Listerine
members.description: Antiseptic mouthwash with a sharp herbal bite.

members.title: Coca-Cola
members.description: Caramel-colored carbonated soft drink.

members.title: Chainsaw
members.description: Motorized saw with teeth mounted on a looping chain.

members.title: Silly Putty
members.description: Bouncy, stretchy silicone putty packaged in a plastic egg.

members.title: Rubik's Cube
members.description: Twisting 3x3x3 puzzle with six colored faces.

intruders.title: Velcro
intruders.description: Two-sided fastener made of tiny hooks and loops.
intruders.why: The idea came from burrs, but it was designed as a fastener from day one. A famous origin story, not a change of purpose.

intruders.title: Band-Aid
intruders.description: Adhesive strip with a small gauze pad for minor cuts.
intruders.why: Invented for exactly this job, covering kitchen cuts. It has a charming origin story but never changed purpose.

theme: Bands named after a song by another artist.
decoy: British and American rock bands with borrowed or cryptic names

members.title: Radiohead
members.description: Oxford band that moved from guitar anthems to glitchy electronics.

members.title: The Rolling Stones
members.description: London blues-rock band fronted by Mick Jagger for six decades.

members.title: Deep Purple
members.description: Hard-rock pioneers behind a famous riff about a fire on Lake Geneva.

members.title: Judas Priest
members.description: Birmingham metal band known for twin lead guitars and leather-and-studs.

members.title: The Pretty Things
members.description: Raw 1960s R&B band that went on to make an early rock opera.

members.title: Death Cab for Cutie
members.description: Washington State indie band fronted by Ben Gibbard.

members.title: The Sisters of Mercy
members.description: Leeds gothic-rock band built around a drum machine called Doktor Avalanche.

members.title: Pretenders
members.description: Chrissie Hynde's band, formed in London in the late 1970s.

intruders.title: The Doors
intruders.description: Los Angeles band whose singer styled himself the Lizard King.
intruders.why: Named after Aldous Huxley's book 'The Doors of Perception', which is a book, not a song.

intruders.title: Duran Duran
intruders.description: Birmingham new-wave band famous for glossy, exotic music videos.
intruders.why: Named after a villain in the film 'Barbarella', which is a film, not a song.

theme: Objects named after the person who actually invented them.
decoy: Eponymous objects, meaning things named after a person

members.title: Diesel engine
members.description: Compression-ignition engine that runs without a spark plug.

members.title: Ferris wheel
members.description: Giant upright rotating wheel carrying passenger cars.

members.title: Petri dish
members.description: Shallow lidded glass dish for growing cultures.

members.title: Tupperware
members.description: Plastic food containers with an airtight 'burping' seal.

members.title: Jacuzzi
members.description: Hot tub whose jets pump bubbling water.

members.title: Zeppelin
members.description: Rigid airship with gas cells inside a metal frame.

members.title: Stetson
members.description: Wide-brimmed felt hat associated with the American West.

members.title: Braille
members.description: Tactile writing system of raised dots.

intruders.title: Guillotine
intruders.description: Tall frame whose weighted, angled blade drops between two uprights.
intruders.why: Named after Joseph-Ignace Guillotin, who argued for its use but did not design it. Antoine Louis and Tobias Schmidt built it.

intruders.title: Cardigan
intruders.description: Knitted sweater that opens down the front with buttons.
intruders.why: Named after the 7th Earl of Cardigan, who made it fashionable but did not invent it.
